headline: Evans survives match darts to beat Crabtree
standfirst: Ricky Evans won a last-leg decider at the Grand Slam, then described a season in which playing had become a chore.
body: Ricky Evans came through a last-leg decider against Cam Crabtree, winning 5-4 in his opening Grand Slam of Darts group match and surviving multiple match darts along the way.

Crabtree had lost 5-1 to James Wade in his first game, so had little room for error. Evans said he expected his younger opponent to play the spoiler. He called the win gritty and admitted it was the kind of game he normally loses.
He was not happy with his own standard, saying the pressure had got to him a little, but he felt he held his nerve at the end. "Stats mean nothing," he said. "Just win."

The more striking comments came when he discussed his year. A run of ProTour defeats had left him outside the automatic World Championship places, and he said he had endured "11 months of pure hatred" towards the game. He described darts as having become a chore rather than a hobby, and said he had stopped playing county darts and was trying to quit local league darts.

Evans linked the change to life away from the oche. He said he now has a relationship and plans for a settled home, so a bad result no longer leaves him with nowhere to go. He said he is falling out of love with travelling and living out of a suitcase.
Qualifying for the Grand Slam, he said, has helped him enjoy playing again.
